basis.title: What is this based on?
basis.body: The questions are adapted from the public-domain IPIP item pool. Your answers form a profile across five axes of tendency; the archetype is the name given to the description that profile falls closest to.
basis.limits: Limits: a short form is low resolution, it carries self-report bias, and the borders between archetypes are not sharp. An archetype name is an editorial reading, not a scientific category.

scale.heading: The scale
scale.body: The questions come from the public-domain IPIP item pool. Five axes are measured: openness to experience, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness and emotional steadiness. Each has four items, half of them reverse-keyed, so that agreeing your way down the list does not build a profile out of nothing.

adaptation.heading: The two versions
adaptation.body: The Turkish items are not word-for-word translations. Phrases that read as forced in Turkish were replaced with everyday sentences asking about the same behaviour. That means neither version can be compared against international norms: each is consistent within itself and not against anything outside it.

matching.heading: How an archetype is picked
matching.body: Your answers become a point in five dimensions, and that point is matched to whichever of the eighteen archetypes it lands nearest to — nearest point, not first threshold crossed. So a profile sitting between two archetypes settles on the one it is genuinely closer to rather than on whichever gate it happened to pass first.

limits.heading: Limits
limits.body:
A short form is coarse: twenty items separate an axis into a few steps, not into fine grades.

Self-report is biased. People mark themselves not as they are but as they would like to be that day; mood moves the result.

The borders between archetypes are not sharp. For a profile sitting between two of them there is no "right" answer, only a nearer one.

An archetype label is an editorial reading, not a scientific category. It turns a five-dimensional profile into a name you can read; it is not a diagnosis, a measure of ability, or a personality type.
